RE: First-Level Appeal of Adverse Benefit Determination
Reference Number: POC-1ACF427871-17933
Member: Casey Iverson — Member ID: W207784190
Plan: Fidelis Care (Commercial/ACA), New York
Requested Service: Partial knee replacement — CPT 27446
Date of Notice: 2026-08-25
Appeal Deadline: 2027-02-21
Treating Surgeon: Marchetti, MD, Orthopedic Surgery [practice name/NPI/phone – to be added]

To the Appeals and Grievances Department:

I am appealing the denial of prior authorization for CPT 27446 (partial/unicompartmental knee arthroplasty) reflected in the notice dated 2026-08-25, reference number POC-1ACF427871-17933. The stated reason for denial was: "the imaging findings submitted do not support the medical necessity of the requested procedure."

Fidelis Care's own provider materials state that prior authorization and medical-necessity review of knee arthroplasty procedures, including CPT 27446, for Qualified Health Plan/Ambetter from Fidelis Care members is performed by Evolent (formerly National Imaging Associates, Inc./NIA) under Evolent's Musculoskeletal Surgery Guidelines. The specific chapter addressing this procedure is the "Evolent Clinical Guideline for Knee Arthroplasty" (Guideline Number Evolent_CG_1763, formerly NIA_CG_311). I request that Fidelis Care and/or Evolent identify, in writing, the exact version and effective date of that guideline that was actually applied to this denial, and provide a copy of it, so that we can confirm our submission addresses the current criteria. The quotations below are drawn from a published copy of that same Evolent guideline; because I could not confirm that Fidelis Care's own hosted copy is identically worded to the version applied in this case, I am asking Fidelis Care to verify these are the controlling criteria before finalizing the appeal decision.

1. Denial reason vs. the imaging in the record

The submitted MRI of the knee, dated 2026-07-30, shows "full-thickness cartilage loss in the medial compartment with bone-on-bone apposition" and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially. I understand the guideline's unicompartmental knee arthroplasty section states the radiographic requirement as: "Weight-bearing radiographs demonstrate only unicompartmental disease (with or without patellofemoral involvement), described as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or grade 4 degeneration," and separately notes: "MRI should not be the primary radiographic test used to determine the presence or severity of arthritic changes in the joint."

If the stated denial reason is based on the fact that the only imaging submitted was an MRI rather than weight-bearing plain radiographs, we ask that this be clarified, because that is a correctable documentation gap rather than a lack of medical necessity. [Weight-bearing knee radiographs — to be obtained/submitted by Dr. Marchetti's office, or confirmation that they were already taken and simply not forwarded, is being requested as a supplement to this appeal.] The MRI findings of full-thickness, bone-on-bone cartilage loss corroborate advanced unicompartmental disease and should be considered alongside the weight-bearing films once available.

2. General requirements for elective knee arthroplasty

The guideline states: "Elective knee arthroplasty may be considered if the following general criteria are met: Knee pain with documented loss of function, which may include painful weight bearing, painful or inadequate range of motion to accomplish age appropriate activities of daily living (ADLs) and/or employment, and painful mechanical catching, locking, or popping... Individual is medically stable and optimized for surgery... does not have an active local or systemic infection... does not have active, untreated drug dependency... has good oral hygiene and does not have major dental work scheduled or anticipated..."

The record documents: 24 months of progressive knee pain; documented loss of function (patient cannot climb stairs without assistance, wakes 3–4 times nightly with pain); no active infection; no untreated substance use; BMI 29 (not an excessively high BMI); non-smoker (no nicotine addiction). [Dental/oral hygiene status is not addressed in the packet and can be confirmed by the surgeon's office if needed.] These records satisfy the general requirement.

3. Non-operative management

The guideline requires: "Non-operative management must include at least TWO or more of the following unless otherwise specified in clinical indications below: Rest or activity modifications/limitations; Weight reduction for individual with elevated BMI; Protected weight-bearing with cane, walker, or crutches; Brace/orthosis; Physical therapy modalities; Physician-supervised exercise program (including home exercise program); Application of heat or ice; Pharmacologic treatment: oral/topical NSAIDS, acetaminophen, or analgesics; Intra-articular injection(s)."

The record documents at least three of these modalities: (a) supervised physical therapy, 8 weeks, 16 visits (2026-05-14 to 2026-07-09), documented in the PT discharge note; (b) NSAIDs for 4 months with inadequate relief; and (c) a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-03 giving only 4 weeks of partial relief. This exceeds the "at least TWO" threshold.

4. Unicompartmental Knee Arthroplasty (UKA)/Partial Knee Replacement (PKA) criteria

The guideline states: "Medial or lateral UKA/PKA may be medically necessary when ALL of the following criteria are met: At least 12 weeks of pain localized to the medial or lateral compartment; Unless bone-on-bone articulation is present, failure of at least 12 weeks of non-operative treatment...; Total arc of motion (goniometer) > 90 degrees; Normal ACL or stable reconstructed ACL per physical exam test; Contracture ≤ 10 degrees upon physical exam (goniometer); Angular deformity ≤ 10 degrees, passively correctable to neutral upon physical exam (goniometer); Weight-bearing radiographs demonstrate only unicompartmental disease... described as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 3 or grade 4 degeneration... No corticosteroid injection into the joint within 12 weeks of surgery; No prior arthroscopic knee surgery within 6 months of surgery."

Mapping the record to each element:
- Pain duration/localization: 24 months of progressive knee pain, with MRI-confirmed medial compartment disease. [Please confirm in the exam note that pain was clinically localized to the medial compartment, consistent with the MRI findings.]
- Failure of non-operative treatment: documented above (PT, NSAIDs, injection); in addition, the MRI documents bone-on-bone apposition, which the guideline itself treats as an alternative basis that reduces the need to further demonstrate failed conservative care.
- Total arc of motion, ACL stability, contracture, and angular deformity: the exam note documents "range of motion limited by pain" and "positive provocative testing," but does not record the specific goniometric measurements or ACL stability testing results called for by this criterion. [Goniometric arc-of-motion, ACL exam findings, contracture measurement, and angular deformity measurement are being requested from Dr. Marchetti's office and will be submitted as a supplement to this appeal.]
- Imaging: MRI dated 2026-07-30 documents Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 changes medially with full-thickness, bone-on-bone cartilage loss. [Weight-bearing knee radiographs, if not already in the file, are being obtained and will be submitted to satisfy the specific imaging modality referenced in the guideline.]
- Corticosteroid injection timing: the injection was administered 2026-05-03. [Surgery date to be confirmed], but as of the date of this appeal, well more than 12 weeks have elapsed since that injection, satisfying the "no injection within 12 weeks of surgery" requirement.
- Prior arthroscopic surgery: the packet contains no record of arthroscopic surgery on the affected knee. [Please confirm with the surgeon's office that no arthroscopic procedure has been performed within 6 months of the proposed surgery date.]

5. Contraindications

The guideline lists contraindications including "Local or systemic active infection," "Inflammatory arthritis," "Angular deformity or contracture greater than indicated range," "Significant arthritic involvement of opposite compartment," "ACL instability," "Poor bone quality or significant osteoporosis or osteopenia," and "Meniscectomy of the opposite compartment, involving > 25% of meniscus." Nothing in the submitted record indicates the presence of any of these contraindications. [If the surgeon's chart addresses the opposite (lateral) compartment or ACL status directly, please include that documentation with the supplemental submission described above.]

Requested Action

We ask that Fidelis Care and Evolent reconsider the denial of CPT 27446 in light of the clinical documentation summarized above, and that the reviewer specify precisely which element(s) of the applicable Knee Arthroplasty guideline were found unmet, so that any remaining documentation gap (e.g., weight-bearing radiographs, goniometric measurements, ACL exam findings) can be promptly supplied by Dr. Marchetti's office. We are submitting this appeal well within the 180-day deadline stated in the notice (due by 2027-02-21) and request written confirmation of receipt and the applicable review timeframe.

Please direct all correspondence regarding this appeal to the address/phone number above, and to Dr. Marchetti's office at [phone/fax] for any additional clinical records needed.

Sincerely,

Casey Iverson
Member ID: W207784190

Enclosures: Physical therapy discharge note (2026-05-14 to 2026-07-09); medication/injection records; MRI report dated 2026-07-30; [weight-bearing knee radiographs, if available]; [additional exam findings, if available]; copy of Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-25.
